definitions.process: A business process is a structured set of activities or tasks that produces a specific service or product for a particular customer or market.
definitions.application: An application is a software system that supports one or more business processes by providing specific functionality.
definitions.informationObject: An information object is a logical concept representing a type of business data — e.g. an invoice, customer record, or order.
definitions.informationSource: An information source is the physical or logical system that stores and provides access to information objects — e.g. a database or module.
definitions.technologyComponent: A technology component is the underlying infrastructure — servers, cloud services, databases, or platforms — that applications run on.
definitions.server: A server is a single installation – physical, virtual or in the cloud – that technology components and applications run on, e.g. an alarm server.
definitions.connection: A connection represents a relationship between two objects — e.g. an application supporting a process or running on a technology component.
definitions.serverService: A server service is a service delivered from the servers, e.g. external DNS or the network (LAN/WiFi). The list comes from Servertjänster in the integration platform.

domainOverview.title: Domain — the BDAT model
domainOverview.subtitle: Business · Information · Application · Technology
domainOverview.heading: Four layers that hang together
domainOverview.intro1: The EA portal describes the organisation's architecture in four layers following the BDAT model. Each layer answers its own question: business answers why, information answers what, applications answer how and technology answers with what.
domainOverview.intro2: Business sets the direction through its processes — what we actually do. Information is what the business handles: the concepts, the information objects and the sources they are stored in. Applications are the support that does the work, and technology is the platform they run on.
domainOverview.intro3: Every object in the portal belongs to one of the layers, and it is the connections between the layers that make it possible to answer questions such as "which applications support this process?" or "which information is affected if this server goes away?". Pick a layer in the pyramid or a card below to explore that domain.
domainOverview.pyramidCaption: Click a layer to jump to that domain

access.title: Access
access.intro: Decide who sees and may do what with the architecture objects. A grant gives someone a role – everyone signed in, a global role, a group or a user – over all objects, some object types or a single object. A grant on a process can cover all its sub-processes. Grants only give rights, they never take any away. Administrators always have full access.
